accepted_claims: The weighted Hilbert shift on H is invertible and bicyclic, with forward norm 1, inverse norm exp(sqrt(n)), and empty adjoint point spectrum.

The Banach augmentation-ideal operator T on I={f in A: f(1)=0} is invertible and bicyclic, with forward norm 1, log inverse norm divided by sqrt(n) tending to 1, and adjoint point spectrum exactly the unit circle minus {1}.
For every 0<a<1/8, the explicit L_a are bounded on A and H and annihilate the entire cutoff classes and their closures J_A and J_H.
The A-distance from z-1 to J_A is at least 15/8192. Both I/J_A and H/J_H are infinite-dimensional.
Nonzero localized cutoff elements exist, and the hull of J_A is exactly {1}.
The induced operator on I/J_A is cyclic, with cyclic vector z-1+J_A.
The strict inclusion J_A in I obstructs the cutoff-density identification of the subendpoint method, without establishing noncyclicity of either full model.
boundaries: The original counterexample-or-universal-cyclicity problem is not resolved by this submission.
Cyclicity of the full augmentation-ideal Banach operator remains undetermined here.
Cyclicity of the full weighted Hilbert model remains undetermined here.
The defect quotient is cyclic; its infinite dimension and the proper cutoff ideal do not give a noncyclic counterexample.
The spectral hypothesis is noncontainment of the whole unit circle in the adjoint point spectrum, not disjointness.
The functional parameter is strictly 0<a<1/8; no endpoint a=1/8 summability assertion is made.
The bound 15/8192 is a lower bound, not an exact distance.
Atzmon 1980 is credited for the underlying classical endpoint ideal phenomenon; no novelty or priority claim is made.
The 2007 note and relevant 1980 and original-report portions were inspected. The 2008 full text was not retrieved, inspected, or used.
No exhaustive literature search or present global-open-status certificate is claimed.
